cells.title: Install picked design packs on plugin-first onboarding too
cells.action:
RED FIRST: write the failing tests in onboard/tests.rs before the code and watch each fail for its own reason.

Plugin-first onboarding sets `sync_skills: !args.plugin_source,` (mod.rs:419), and plan.rs `let skill_sync = if opts.sync_skills {` (:1242) then plans no skill targets at all, so a plugin-first host never receives its picked design packs (owner decision 1dd050b7). Make plugin-first onboarding still plan and apply the DESIGN source only: when sync_skills is false and a pick exists, compute the repo skill-home targets for `bee-design` plus each picked `bee-design-<pack>` from the design root (the same SkillSources pick logic dob-3 added), and prune un-picked `bee-design*` dirs; in plugin-first no other skill is copied, refreshed or removed. With no pick (absent or "none"), plugin-first writes and removes nothing design-related except pruning `bee-design*` dirs when the pick is "none". Also add `--design-packs <list|none>` to the onboard usage line in router.rs (around the onboard entry, ~:99-101).

Tests: plugin-first + --design-packs web --apply writes exactly bee-design and bee-design-web into the repo skill homes and no bee-hive or other bee- skill; plugin-first with no pick writes no skill dir; plugin-first switching web to none removes the design dirs; repo-copy behavior is unchanged (existing dob-3 tests stay green).

truths: each new test fails first for its own reason
a plugin-first apply with a pick writes exactly bee-design and the picked packs and no other skill
a plugin-first apply with no pick writes no skill dir

cells.title: Pass the design pick through both installers and show onboarding's notices
cells.action:
RED FIRST: extend packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/tests/installer_contracts.rs (model: `fn both_installers_onboard_from_the_source_and_vendor_before_applying() {` at :371) before changing the scripts, and watch each new assertion fail for its own reason.

(1) install.sh: add `--design-packs <list|none>` to argument parsing and the usage text; when given, append `--design-packs <value>` to ONBOARD_FLAGS beside `ONBOARD_FLAGS+=("--no-statusline")` (:474) so the plan, apply and recheck calls all carry it. (2) install.ps1: add a `-DesignPacks <list|none>` parameter and append `--design-packs <value>` to `$onboardFlags` beside `if ($NoStatusline) { $onboardFlags += '--no-statusline' }` (:545). (3) Notices: after a successful onboard apply, each installer prints onboard's notices (the plan JSON's notices array, or the apply output's `notice:` lines) to the user, so the design offer and other offers are seen; today install.sh keeps `$APPLY_OUTPUT` and prints it only on failure (`printf '%s\n' "$APPLY_OUTPUT" >&2` at :743). (4) README.md and INSTALL.md: document the flag in the installer options where the other onboard pass-through flags are listed. (5) scripts/install.sh and install.ps1 are release inventory roots: rewrite the release manifest with `bee dev release-manifest --write`. No comments added to the scripts beyond what already exists (repo rule: no new comments).

Tests: install.sh with --design-packs web onto a sandbox target forwards the flag (the target's .bee/config.json records design.packs ["web"] and its skill homes hold bee-design and bee-design-web); a target with an index.html and no pick sees the design offer text in the installer output; install.ps1 carries -DesignPacks into its onboard flags (string-level contract check if pwsh is absent, as the existing ps1 contracts do).

truths: each new assertion fails first for its own reason
install.sh --design-packs web onto a sandbox target installs bee-design and bee-design-web and records the pick
a target with UI files and no pick shows the design offer in installer output
README and INSTALL document the flag

-DesignPacks parameter forwarded to onboard, notices printed

key_links: the flag reaches every onboard call the installer makes (plan, apply, recheck)
